report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** Add-on *pharmaceutical-grade* cannabidiol reduces convulsive-seizure frequency in children/adolescents with treatment-resistant Dravet syndrome, compared with placebo, when used alongside existing antiseizure treatment.

In a 14-week randomized, double-blind trial of 120 patients aged 2–18, median convulsive seizures fell from 12.4 to 5.9 per month with cannabidiol, versus 14.9 to 14.1 with placebo (median reduction 39% vs 13%). A larger 199-patient randomized trial replicated benefit: convulsive-seizure frequency fell 48.7% with 10 mg/kg/day and 45.7% with 20 mg/kg/day, versus 26.9% with placebo. The evidence therefore directly supports the claim for prescribed add-on cannabidiol, not over-the-counter CBD products.

Harms matter: somnolence/sedation, reduced appetite, diarrhoea, and liver-enzyme elevations occur; monitoring and attention to interactions (especially with clobazam/valproate) are needed. U.S. labeling indicates cannabidiol for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients aged ≥1 year.

- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7052786/
